title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
summary: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.

title: A matrix model of an M5--brane on a plane--wave background
summary: We construct the maximally supersymmetric deformation of the recently proposed $\mathcal{A}_6$ matrix model on a plane--wave background. We derive the same theory independently, by reducing the light--cone M5--brane on a five--sphere in this background to its lowest harmonics, including the dynamics of its chiral two--form and of its fermions. We then classify all its classical vacua. We show that one of them is the fivebrane giant graviton, and that its fluctuations form a single $\mathfrak{su}(2|4)$ multiplet, which reproduces the $\ell=1$ level of the spherical transverse fivebrane identified in the large $N$ limit of BMN theory. Moreover, the dynamical tensor supports new families of vacua, where the flux balances the size of the brane, and whose spectrum contains that of a fuzzy membrane. Finally, we show that BLG theory sits inside the model, both on a Coulomb branch of the massless theory and around the giant graviton of the massive one, where the two membranes are polarized into the fivebrane.

title: Onset of quantum chaos in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories
summary: We exhibit random matrix statistics in the scaling dimensions of non-BPS primary operators in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories. Specifically, we consider the sigma model with K3 target space and $\mathcal N=(4,4)$ supersymmetry in a neighborhood of the Kummer orbifold point $\mathbb T^4/\mathbb Z_2$. At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. The exactly marginal blow-up deformations that preserve this symmetry form a four-dimensional space, whose directions we parametrize by unit quaternions. Along each deformation direction, we compute the first-order splitting of the degenerate levels, i.e., the leading anomalous dimensions as the coupling goes to zero. In sectors where all exact symmetries are resolved, including a hidden $\mathbb Z_2$ at the even levels, the non-zero first-order shifts along a generic direction follow the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE), as we verify by computing several spectral diagnostics. We compare quantitatively with the well-known singlet deformation, which has enhanced symmetry: even after all its known symmetries are resolved, its first-order spectrum has exact degeneracies, its gap ratio approaches the GOE value only slowly as the energy increases, and its unfolded spectrum lacks the long-range rigidity of the GOE.

title: Energy and Charge Transmission at Conformal Interfaces: Relations and Bounds
summary: Symmetry constrains how independently energy and charge can pass through a conformal interface. For interfaces between Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) models $G_{k_L}$ and $G_{k_R}$ preserving the diagonal affine algebra, we derive an exact relation between the energy and charge transmission coefficients, $c_{LR}=2(\dim G)k_{LR}/(k_L+k_R+2h^\vee)$. Together with positivity of outgoing energy, this relation excludes complete energy transmission at unequal levels. With additional bulk degrees of freedom, the equality is replaced by bounds controlled by the coset central charges. Complete transmission from a lower-level WZW model then imposes a lower bound on the coset central charge on the other side. In linear response, the relation fixes the ratio of thermal to charge conductance to the harmonic mean of the two bulk ratios, independently of the interface, while coset sectors bound the thermal conductance at fixed charge conductance. This interface-independent ratio is a generalized Wiedemann--Franz law for conformal interfaces between WZW models. The charge transmission coefficient $k_{LR}$ also governs equilibrium charge fluctuations and fixes the leading quadratic dependence of the boundary-condition-changing operator's scaling dimension on the rotation angle.

title: Perturbative $S$-matrix Unitarity in Higher-Derivative Theory of Fermions
summary: We construct a higher-derivative fermion theory with four-Fermi interactions. In quantum field theory, it is conjectured that good high-energy behavior of tree-level scattering amplitudes implies renormalizability, a notion referred to as the tree-unitarity criterion. To investigate whether this criterion is satisfied in a higher-derivative fermion theory, we examine the structure of the $S$-matrix in detail. Owing to the higher-derivative kinetic term, the mass dimension of the spinor field differs from that of a conventional fermion, rendering four-Fermi interactions renormalizable at the cost of introducing ghost states. We show that, unlike bosonic ghosts, fermionic ghosts inevitably give rise to negative-norm states regardless of the sign of their energy eigenvalues. We further demonstrate that, in contrast to conventional four-Fermi theories, the higher-derivative four-Fermi theory satisfies perturbative $S$-matrix unitarity. In light of the tree-unitarity criterion, these results provide supporting evidence for the renormalizability of higher-derivative fermion theories and generalize our previous findings on higher-derivative scalar theories to the fermionic case.

title: String breaking in a (1+1)-dimensional $e^+e^-$ collider
summary: In this paper, we develop a framework for studying solitons in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories using tensor networks, and we apply it to simulate $e^+e^-$ collisions in the massive Schwinger model. We work at $\theta = \pi$ and at a bare fermion mass exceeding the critical value; in this regime, there are two degenerate vacua, and the $e^+$ and $e^-$ particles are realized as soliton states interpolating between them. We carefully explain how to find and characterize such soliton states using infinite tensor network methods, and then exhibit real-time simulations of their collisions. These collisions involve the formation of an energetic flux string, and we demonstrate that our final states are superpositions of elastic and string-breaking trajectories.

title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
summary: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}\mathbf{A'}$, a general class of topoloical orders, as the $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$-extended symmetry topological field theory. We also conjecture a series of underlying (unexplored) modular invariants, connecting the conformal embedding and the pairing.

title: Neural variational Skyrmions as a topological benchmark: emergent symmetry, precision energies and KAN--MLP comparison
comment: 32 pages, 6 figures, 12 tables. Code and data: this https URL
summary: We propose the three-dimensional Skyrme model as a topological benchmark for neural variational methods and construct fully three-dimensional Skyrmions with baryon number $B=1,\ldots,4$ without imposing a symmetry ansatz, with high precision. For $B=2,3,4$, the relaxation of these Skyrmions starts from $B$ unit-charge lumps with random positions and orientations, which carry no symmetry information. The known toroidal, tetrahedral, and cubic Skyrmions nevertheless emerge spontaneously. The resulting variational energies for $B=1,\ldots,4$ lie slightly below the published reference values. The neural method highlights the high accuracy for retaining the topological charge, differing from $B$ by at most $10^{-6}$ in the highest-precision solutions. Our numerical method goes through physical constraint tests such as the Derrick virial relation and the Faddeev--Bogomolny bound, together with evaluation / verification through independent quadratures and resolution sweeps. We then compare Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs) with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) in more than a thousand training runs, both with and without a rational-map ansatz. With default settings, KANs appear markedly superior, but most of the gap disappears once the MLP activation function and learning rate are tuned. KANs remain more parameter-efficient and more robust at fixed epoch budget, while MLPs with the tuned activation function perform at least as well at fixed wall-clock time. We also argue that continuous gradient descent cannot smoothly change the topological sector of our neural field, clarifying the origin of topological freezing observed in our neural variational solvers. Our results on the neural methods applied to Skyrmions pave a research ground for AI-agentic benchmarks for classical topological solitons, toward AI-assisted soliton physics.

title: Gauging background isometries of the ILST null string
summary: We present a general gauging of a subalgebra, $\mathfrak h$, of the isometries $\mathfrak g$ of the background geometry for the ILST string (e-Print: hep-th/9307108 [hep-th]). We discuss which of the isometries in $\mathfrak g$ survive the gauging as symmetries. The gauged symmetry does not in general involve transformations of the vector density V. There is thus a corresponding contraction of the algebra of constraints as compared to the flat background and it no longer represent the full Carroll-Weyl algebra. This algebra of constraints is derived and discussed, partly in an appendix. The gauging of isometries sets the stage for a reduction, or quotient construction, leading to a new null string on the space of orbits of the gauge group. We illustrate this by deriving the ILST string in $AdS$ background as a quotient of a model in SO(d,2) background by a SO(d,1) isometry, in group space

title: The $a$-function in fractional dimensions
summary: We consider the $\beta$-functions for both scalar, and supersymmetric chiral scalar, field theories with a general $n$th-order self-interaction, in their critical dimensions, which are in general non-integer. We perform a full computation up to fourth order in the coupling in the supersymmetric case, and a partial one in the scalar case. We then demonstrate the existence of an $a$-function, related to the $\beta$-functions by a gradient flow with a positive-definite metric, through fourth order in the coupling in the supersymmetric case; and show that all our fourth-order results in the scalar case are consistent with a similar property holding there too.

title: Polarized IKKT holography: bulk realization of BPS operators
summary: We study the holographic imprint of polarization in the lowest BPS multiplet of the IKKT matrix model. On the matrix model side, the deformation requires operator mixing and broken-symmetry Ward identities to organize the surviving operators into an irreducible atypical multiplet of the $F(4)$ superalgebra. In the bulk, we use one-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity to identify the analytic half-BPS background with $F(4)$ symmetry whose boundary behavior matches the IKKT polarization. We solve the linearized bosonic and fermionic equations around this background and its undeformed counterpart exactly, and extract the independent asymptotic data. The supersymmetry transformations of these data reproduce the matrix model multiplets, thus establishing a bulk realization of this BPS operator structure.

title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
summary: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS fluxes. Deriving the BMS charges requires additional care, since BMS generators extended into the bulk are generally not tangent to the null hypersurfaces. After accounting for this and the associated anomalies, the renormalized canonical charges still contain an additional soft contribution. The prescription of a covariant boundary Lagrangian determines a corner improvement that removes this term and recovers the standard BMS charges.

title: Banana D-modules
summary: We study the holonomic $D$-module whose solutions are generic-mass banana Feynman integrals with complex propagator powers and spacetime dimension. We call this the banana $D$-module. Two properties of the banana $D$-module are studied: its holonomic rank and the irreducibility of the monodromy representation. This is achieved by relating the banana $D$-module to Lauricella $F_{C}$ hypergeometric systems. Further, we expand the generic-mass banana Feynman integral and the associated discontinuity integral in terms of series solutions. Finally, we analyze the Pfaffian system arising from the banana $D$-module and construct an explicit $d\log$ representation in the equal-mass specialization.

title: The Kerr Metric in Canonical Harmonic Coordinates to All Orders
comment: 36 pages. Codes available at Github this https URL and Zenodo this https URL
summary: We give in closed form the transformation from Boyer--Lindquist coordinates to the canonical harmonic coordinates of the Kerr metric, to all orders in Newton's constant and in the spin. This is the canonical harmonic chart selected by the MPM prescription and by the harmonic-gauge Einstein recursion sourced by the Kerr multipoles, with the residual homogeneous freedom fixed by the boundary conditions. The chart is the real, time-reversal-covariant combination of the two radial harmonic functions underlying the Cook--Scheel coordinates, which differ from it by a definite residual harmonic transformation. The proof rests on a classification of the residual harmonic freedom. Rotational covariance, parity, time reversal and analyticity in the spin allow a decaying homogeneous solution beyond the linear field only in the spatial components at third post-Minkowskian order, with angular degree $\ell=p+2$ at spin order $a^p$. This sector is a pure gauge mode, equivalent to an MPM gauge moment. The exact chart selects the representative in which this third-PM homogeneous mode vanishes; imposing the same condition on the recursion removes the only residual ambiguity and fixes its solution uniquely. As a consequence, the canonical MPM iteration needs no finite-part regularisation and no harmonicity correction at any order. We give the exact gothic metric and the post-Minkowskian coefficients in closed form through fifth order, where an arctangent function first appears at fourth order. We find agreement with recent canonical MPM and amplitude-based results at fourth order, and we verify the construction in exact arithmetic through fifth order and twelfth order in the spin, with code made publicly available.

title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
summary: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.

title: Bulk Wilson Loops from $\mathscr{I}$
summary: A Carrollian description of four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory on partially complexified future null infinity was recently proposed by Opreij, Skinner and Wang in arXiv:2604.09771. In this paper, we give a new form of the Carrollian Yang-Mills kinetic action on real future null infinity, and recover the logarithmic two-point function found by arXiv:2604.09771. We then extend the Carrollian description of Yang-Mills beyond scattering amplitudes by studying the expectation value of a null polygonal Wilson loop in Minkowski spacetime. We propose a boundary operator given by the trace of a cyclic product of holomorphic frames on the good cuts associated with the polygon's vertices. At order $g^2$, we show analytically that the boundary calculation reproduces the rational bulk integrand obtained from a self-dual Lagrangian insertion.

title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
summary: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

title: Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the exploration of tabletop detectors for GW signals at frequencies comparable to and below the LIGO band, in the idealized limit. By exploiting the trajectory-dependent gravitationally induced phase, the proposed scheme offers a distinct and potentially complementary approach to GW detection and motivates further investigation of its experimental feasibility and practical sensitivity.

title: Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases
summary: Finding bases of Feynman integrals whose differential equations are suitable for phenomenology is a remarkably verifiable task. We exploit this to design two \emph{skills} with which Claude Opus~5.5 produces novel results autonomously, working for several days. For a two-loop five-point family (with two masses and 18 elliptic sectors) and a two-loop superfamily for the radiative jet function with a K3 sector, the agent finds bases whose differential equations are free of poles in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ and at most quadratic in it, and takes the jet-function one to $\varepsilon$-factorized form.

title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
summary: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

title: On a Supersymmetric Generalization of the Matytsin Formula
summary: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup $U(n|m)$ in the limit $n,m\to\infty$ when $n/m$ is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for $U(N)$. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.

title: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
summary: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar curvature region, which prevents the Universe from evolving into the anti-gravity or having a ghost graviton region, without the fine-tuning of the initial conditions. We also discuss how this regime can be tested using peculiar velocity and kSZ effect probes.

title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
summary: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $\lambda$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|\lambda|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|\lambda|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|\lambda|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|\lambda|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $η$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
summary: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.

title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
summary: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the residual strong-coupling mismatch. A selected common-threshold benchmark gives a heavy-state mass of $1.137\times10^{16}$ GeV, a reference crossing of $1.139\times10^{16}$ GeV, and a conditional proton partial lifetime of $8.72\times10^{35}$ years. At a micron-scale gravitational length, suppressed baryon-violating matching amplitudes can satisfy proton limits, although the high-scale mass-matching condition selects a distinct region of the scanned geometry. Independently, a $5$ TeV neutral-vector benchmark yields an inclusive leading-order dielectron cross section of $0.183$ fb over $4.5$--$5.5$ TeV at a collider energy of $13.6$ TeV, before detector selection. The analysis provides quantitative effective-model benchmarks and identifies the remaining high-scale matching and experimental tests.

title: Effective theory of quantum black holes with Kretschmann scalar
comment: 12 pages, 15 figures, under review in European Physical Journal C
summary: We investigate the thermodynamics, quasinormal modes (QNMs), and shadows of the effective theory of quantum black holes (BHs) by expanding the physical constants in terms of the Kretschmann scalar. The resulting effective metric can contain two horizons, which is typical for a quantum-corrected Schwarzschild spacetime. The second-order corrected metric only shifts the first-order corrected metric, allowing investigation of IR phenomena from the pure first-order corrected one. From a thermodynamic point of view, the metric leads to a stable cold remnant with zero entropy, compatible with the third law of thermodynamics. In the perturbation regime, we use massless scalar perturbations to extract the effective potential, QNMs, graybody factor, and total absorption cross section. We show that double-horizon BHs have a double light ring in the potential, and for a certain value $\Omega/\chi^2=0.01,$ the QNMs are similar to the GR case since the horizon is Schwarzschild-like. We also tested the correspondence between the QNMs and the graybody factor, and our results still hold with an error far below $1\%$. Our results also conclude that the higher the frequency, the bigger the cross-section area. For the optical observables, we observe that the opposite sign of $\Omega$ leads to distinct behavior of the BH's photon sphere and shadow radius. The Sagittarius A* shadow radius upper bound from the Event Horizon Telescope observation in the $2\sigma$ and $1\sigma$ significance set the upper limit of the quantum parameter $\Omega$ to $\Omega/\chi^2 \lesssim 0.3649$ and $\Omega/\chi^2 \lesssim 0.0105$, respectively.

title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
summary: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gaußian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand. In combination, we reduce the sampling task for a general class of complex systems to a Gaußian one, and the main computational task is that of computing the PIK. We illustrate the approach with the one-site Hubbard model at arbitrary chemical potential and with $\phi^4$-deformed extensions of it.

title: Soft-photon resummation for low-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders
summary: We present resummed predictions for $e^+e^- \to \mu^+\mu^-(\gamma)$ and $\pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ in the multi-photon soft limit, matched to exact NLO. The resummation is performed within the Yennie-Frautschi-Suura framework at the amplitude level. The initial and final-state contributions are included coherently, and NLO accuracy with finite electron, muon and pion masses is achieved. We present our calculation, its implementation in a fast Fortran Monte Carlo integrator, and compare our predictions with the generators BabaYaga, KKMC, Phokhara and McMule, in scenarios inspired by the energy-scan (CMD) and radiative-return (KLOE, BES III, B factories) experiments. We find agreement with BabaYaga, which includes higher-order corrections through a parton shower, at the per-mille level in the cross-sections, and differences of up to two percent with the soft-photon resummation of KKMC. This work represents an important step towards the validation of Monte Carlo generators for low-energy experiments, and will be released in the upcoming new version of Phokhara.

title: Ohmic warm inflation
comment: 34 pages, 3 figures. Webinar presentation: this https URL
summary: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

title: Higgs Fluctuation Solver in Four Dimensions: Part II-Toward Finite Lattice-to-MS bar Matching in the SU(2) Higgs Extension
summary: We present a lattice-to-MS_bar matching framework for the $SU(2)$-Higgs theory, including Wilson-plaquette and fundamental scalar-link actions, a counter term basis through $\rho^{12}$, audited momentum-dependent lattice vertices, and fixed routings and projectors. At the benchmark $a=0.8$, $m_0^2=\mu_R^2=0.4$, $g_0=0.65$, and $(\lambda,\gamma,\delta)=(-2,0.8,0.08)$, the potential is $V_0(\rho)=\frac{1}{5}\rho^2-\frac{1}{2}\rho^4+\frac{2}{15}\rho^6+\frac{1}{100}\rho^8$. The scalar-only radial matching shifts, ordered as $(\delta m^2,\delta\lambda,\delta\gamma,\delta\delta,\delta c_{10},\delta c_{12})$, are $(2.75293, -1.45119, -2.85120, 0.356724, 1.07432, 6.20492)$ in solver units, with the continuum-renormalized-minus-lattice convention. The Higgs two-point slope gives $\delta Z_H = 0.0329117974 \pm 0.00000036$ (QMC error). We also evaluate gauge-linked four-, six-, and eight-Higgs projections and derive the continuum one-loop gauge two-point tensor. The tensor passes 29 internal checks; at $p^2=0.4$, its total transverse projection is $\Pi_T=-0.01847$ at zero regulator and $-0.01716$ at $\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}}/\mu_R=1/8$, while the regulator-induced longitudinal projection is $\Pi_L=1.04\times 10^{-5}$ at $\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}}/\mu_R=1/32$. These results establish a tested foundation and quantitative benchmarks for the matching program. The gauge-linked projections remain preliminary, and full gauge-sector matching and Ward-Slavnov-Taylor closure are needed before a matched $SU(2)$ decay prefactor can be claimed.

title: Optimized solver algorithms for computing $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures. To be published in the proceedings of LATTICE 2026
summary: Estimating the trace of the inverse of a large quark matrix is a longstanding problem in lattice QCD. The standard approach is Hutchinson's method, which uses random noise vectors to estimate the trace to a desired statistical tolerance. Each noise vector $b$ requires solving a system of linear equations $Ax = b$. In this work, we introduce a new class of Krylov solvers for this task, called Twin methods. Twin methods generate the Krylov polynomial once then reuse it on all other right-hand sides. This reduces the number of basic linear algebra operations in the algorithm and therefore lowers the trace computation time. We apply the Twin approach to BiCG and BiCGStab and test them on lattice QCD matrices of varying size and in a range of computing contexts. We also present a more economical estimation of $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$ which implements a polynomial approximation of $A^{-1}$ and a singular value deflation. In this scheme, the solvers are applied to only a few noise vectors, and the remainder are treated by the polynomial and the deflation. In our tests, the polynomial approximation combined with the deflation yield a 17-fold speedup in the time required to compute the trace over standard Hutchinson's method.

title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $η$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
summary: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.

title: From Resonance Properties to High-Energy Behavior: The $R$ Ratio from Lattice QCD
summary: We investigate resonance properties and inclusive spectral behavior through Bayesian reconstruction of the $R$-ratio from Euclidean lattice correlators near the physical pion mass. Without additional Gaussian smearing, the reconstructed spectrum already captures the smooth high-energy behavior observed in experiment. Direct integration of the $\rho$ peak determines $f_\rho$ with approximately $1\%$ statistical precision and close agreement with the experimental reference, providing access to resonance properties without resolving individual finite-volume levels. With a common Gaussian width of $\sigma=0.6$~GeV, the lattice and experimental $R$-ratios show good overall agreement over $0.25$--$2.50$~GeV. Comparisons among ensembles with spatial extents up to approximately $10$~fm demonstrate that finite-volume effects can be controlled across these complementary observables. These results demonstrate a unified framework for studying resonance and inclusive physics from lattice QCD, with potential applications to other hadronic channels, inclusive decay rates, and hadronic tensors.

title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
summary: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gaußian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand. In combination, we reduce the sampling task for a general class of complex systems to a Gaußian one, and the main computational task is that of computing the PIK. We illustrate the approach with the one-site Hubbard model at arbitrary chemical potential and with $\phi^4$-deformed extensions of it.

title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, contribution to the Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea
summary: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.

title: Evidence for Y-shaped color confinement of fully heavy baryons
summary: The geometry of color confinement in baryons remains a fundamental question in quantum chromodynamics. We investigate whether heavy-quark spectroscopy can distinguish a genuine three-body Y-shaped confining interaction from a sum of pairwise $\Delta$-shaped interaction. Using a high-precision three-body Schrödinger solver, we perform a simultaneous analysis of experimentally measured bottomonium masses and lattice-QCD calculations of $\Omega_{bbb}$ excitation energies. For each confinement scenario, interaction parameters are independently optimized against the combined spectra. We find that the Y-shaped potential provides a consistent description of both systems, whereas the $\Delta$-shaped potential exhibits significant discrepancies. Our results provide spectroscopic evidence favoring a collective three-body confining interaction and establish triply-heavy baryon spectroscopy as a complementary probe of the nonperturbative geometry of color confinement.

title: String breaking in a (1+1)-dimensional $e^+e^-$ collider
summary: In this paper, we develop a framework for studying solitons in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories using tensor networks, and we apply it to simulate $e^+e^-$ collisions in the massive Schwinger model. We work at $\theta = \pi$ and at a bare fermion mass exceeding the critical value; in this regime, there are two degenerate vacua, and the $e^+$ and $e^-$ particles are realized as soliton states interpolating between them. We carefully explain how to find and characterize such soliton states using infinite tensor network methods, and then exhibit real-time simulations of their collisions. These collisions involve the formation of an energetic flux string, and we demonstrate that our final states are superpositions of elastic and string-breaking trajectories.

title: Quark dipole operators in the gradient-flow scheme at NNLO QCD
summary: Conversion factors for the dimension-five QCD operator basis from the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ to the gradient-flow scheme are presented through NNLO in the strong coupling. In the CP-even sector, the results are provided for general quark masses and arbitrary flavor content of the operators. Specifically, this concerns the quark CMDM operator and its mixing with lower-dimensional QCD operators. In the massless case, our results immediately apply to the quark chromoelectric dipole operator. As a by-product, we also determine missing entries in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ anomalous dimension matrix of the CMDM operator to NNLO QCD.

title: Dijet production in $e^+e^-$ collisions at NNLO+PS accuracy
summary: We present the first complete Monte Carlo event generator with next-to-next-to-leading order QCD accuracy for lepton collisions. The approach is based on a new formulation of the MiNNLO formalism and is applied to dijet production. Starting from the resummation of the three-jet resolution variable $y_3$, we present the corresponding MiNNLO master formula and implement it within the Powheg framework. We discuss phenomenological results relevant for LEP and future electron-positron colliders.

title: Study of Radiative Muon Capture Experimental Data and its Implications for Muon-Conversion Experiments
summary: Radiative muon capture (RMC) is an important background in searches for the neutrinoless conversion of a muon into an electron in the field of a nucleus, and in particular in searches for the lepton flavor and lepton number violating process of muon-to-positron conversion. The high-energy tail of the RMC photon spectrum remains theoretically understudied, leading to large uncertainties in background predictions for upcoming muon-conversion experiments. In this work, we revisit previously published RMC data to investigate improved modeling of the high-energy tail. We develop a model characterized by distinct nucleon-knockout final states, each with its associated multibody phase space and kinematic endpoint. This framework is applied to photon data from TRIUMF and positron data from SINDRUM II, and the results are compared to the previously used closure approximation. We find that separately modeling the distinct nucleon-knockout final states provides an improved description of the available RMC data near the endpoint, and we discuss the implications for the COMET and Mu2e experiments.

title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
summary: We demonstrate that weight-space programming and edits guided by sparse autoencoders can remove unwanted aspects of a particle-physics foundation model through direct edits to its weights. In a foundation model trained on jets, we observe that adding a single soft neutral particle causes large changes in jet classification, violating infrared safety. We locate the responsible attention heads with mechanistic analysis and trace the flaw's origin to pretraining on datasets with different reconstruction thresholds. We then propose two targeted approaches to repair the flaw: by removing three latent directions identified with sparse autoencoders, and by letting language-model agents edit the weights directly, without gradients and with only 50 queries to the model. Both their edits individually remove almost the entire flaw and leave the rest of the model's response nearly unchanged. Compared to fine-tuning, both methods change far fewer parameters. Although built only on $W$ and QCD jets, the edits carry over to all signal classes, the pretrained generator, and a newly trained regression head.

title: Mass Spectra and Radiative Decay Widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\)
summary: Inspired by recent experimental reports on the radiative decay \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma\) and the branching-fraction ratio \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma]\), we investigate the mass spectra and radiative decay widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D_{s1}'(2536)^+\). Within the chiral quark model combined with the Gaussian Expansion Method, the mass spectra obtained agree reasonably well with the experimental data. Besides, the branching-fraction ratio obtained in this work is \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma] = 0.57\) and \(\Gamma(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma) = 3.80\,\mathrm{keV}\). By analyzing our theoretical results against the latest experimental measurements, we conclude that the \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\) can be treated as a mixed state of \(1^1P_1\) and \(1^3P_1\), and it may contain both the \(c\bar{s}\) component and the tetraquark component. In addition, we also obtain \(\Gamma(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma) = 9.14\,\mathrm{keV}\) and \(\Gamma(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma) = 8.59\,\mathrm{keV}\) by treating \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\) as a meson state. More precise experimental data are required to pin down the internal structure of these states.

title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
summary: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the residual strong-coupling mismatch. A selected common-threshold benchmark gives a heavy-state mass of $1.137\times10^{16}$ GeV, a reference crossing of $1.139\times10^{16}$ GeV, and a conditional proton partial lifetime of $8.72\times10^{35}$ years. At a micron-scale gravitational length, suppressed baryon-violating matching amplitudes can satisfy proton limits, although the high-scale mass-matching condition selects a distinct region of the scanned geometry. Independently, a $5$ TeV neutral-vector benchmark yields an inclusive leading-order dielectron cross section of $0.183$ fb over $4.5$--$5.5$ TeV at a collider energy of $13.6$ TeV, before detector selection. The analysis provides quantitative effective-model benchmarks and identifies the remaining high-scale matching and experimental tests.

title: Balancing heavy flavour: Quantum number compensation in the hadronisation of charm and beauty particles in proton-proton collisions
summary: The hadronisation of heavy quarks remains one of the least understood processes of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). While the production of heavy quark pairs can be calculated perturbatively in QCD, the subsequent formation of hadrons involves non-perturbative processes. The description of these processes is predominantly model dependent and sensitive to the underlying mechanisms of colour reconnection and string fragmentation. In particular, the conservation of flavour, baryon number and charge imposes constraints on how heavy-flavour hadrons are formed and balanced within the final state. In this work, we study how the quantum numbers associated with charm and beauty production are balanced in proton-proton collisions, using events simulated with the PYTHIA-8 event generator. Starting from perturbatively produced ($c\overline{c}$) and ($b\overline{b}$) pairs, we examine how the formation of heavy-flavour mesons and baryons, including $D^0$, $B^+$, $\Lambda_c^+$, and $\Lambda_b^0$, is accompanied by compensating particles elsewhere. The analysis focuses on correlations between the identified heavy hadron and the hadronic system responsible for balancing its conserved quantum numbers. We compare three hadronisation configurations that are implemented in PYTHIA: the Monash tune, colour-reconnection models incorporating string junctions (SJ), and close-packing (CP) approaches. We find that the SJ and CP tunes show a substantially enhanced contribution of baryons to the charm and beauty balancing yields compared with the Monash tune; this enhancement becomes more pronounced in high-multiplicity events. This study introduces a framework for characterising quantum-number compensation in heavy-flavour production and provides a new way to test hadronisation dynamics using identified charm- and beauty-hadron correlations, which can be explored at current and future collider experiments.

title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
summary:
It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($\delta$) is 0 or $\pi$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $
u_\mu$ and $
u_	au$, but not the $
u_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sin\delta$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sin\delta$ dependence to be probed in $
u_\mu$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $
u_\mu$ survival probability.

title: Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the exploration of tabletop detectors for GW signals at frequencies comparable to and below the LIGO band, in the idealized limit. By exploiting the trajectory-dependent gravitationally induced phase, the proposed scheme offers a distinct and potentially complementary approach to GW detection and motivates further investigation of its experimental feasibility and practical sensitivity.

title: Type-II quasinormal modes of dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg AdS black holes
summary: In this paper, we investigate Type-II quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a magnetically charged dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg black hole in anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. The Type-II includes coupled gravitational, dilaton and electromagnetic perturbations. Its coupled equations are derived for $\ell=0,1,2$ modes and the QNM frequencies are calculated by employing direct integration and Chebyshev pseudospectral methods, giving consistent results. For nondegenerate dipole ($\ell=1$) mode at fixed curvature, the nonlinear correction starts at order $Q^2$ for electromagnetic-led branch and at order $Q^4$ for scalar-led branch. In this case, stronger AdS curvature enhances reduction of the electromagnetic-led real frequency for positive coupling, while gravitational-led quadrupole real frequency changes weakly with charge. As the curvature weakens, the dipole frequencies approach the AdS normal-mode scale and their damping decreases. We find that all modes computed have negative imaginary parts for nonextremal black holes, implying this black hole is stable against Type-II perturbations. Furthermore, we explore the connection between thermodynamic phase transition and QNMs for $\ell=0$ dilaton. For a subcritical isobaric process, the QNM real frequency of $\ell=0$ dilaton decreases with increasing temperature of small black holes, while it increases with increasing temperature of large black holes. At coexistence, the damping rate for large black holes is about 4.28 times that for small black holes.

title: Microscopic Cosmological Backreaction of an Ultralight Majoron Coupled to a Coherent Hidden Pseudo-Dirac Ensemble
summary: We develop a microscopic framework for the cosmological backreaction of a hidden pseudo-Dirac fermion ensemble derivatively coupled to an ultralight Majoron. Starting from the effective action, we derive the exact operator Ward identity for the pseudo-Dirac current and the associated microscopic energy-transfer law. For a thermal density matrix prepared at a finite initial time, we calculate the subsequent collisionless, linearized coherence response without assuming continued thermal equilibrium or introducing phenomenological dissipation. The finite-time retarded solution retains the initial boundary transient and nonlocal memory contribution, allowing us to assess the validity of the leading local adiabatic approximation and distinguish reversible coherent energy exchange from dissipative friction. For a subdominant Majoron benchmark evolving in a prescribed FRW background, the local energy-transfer rate changes sign, while the present-day fractional velocity correction is only $+5.23\times10^{-53}$. A convergence-tested numerical comparison, including the initial transient and memory contribution, bounds the difference between the retarded and local fractional velocity corrections to less than $6.78\times10^{-17}$ of the local correction. Within the linearized, collisionless positive-energy two-state approximation, these results demonstrate that the microscopic backreaction does not produce significant Majoron freezing for the benchmark considered, while leaving open different behavior in other parameter regimes or preparation histories.

title: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
summary: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar curvature region, which prevents the Universe from evolving into the anti-gravity or having a ghost graviton region, without the fine-tuning of the initial conditions. We also discuss how this regime can be tested using peculiar velocity and kSZ effect probes.

title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
summary: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $\lambda$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|\lambda|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|\lambda|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|\lambda|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|\lambda|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
summary: We investigate how matter fields affect spacetime regularity in a class of gravitational theories with second-order field equations in spherical symmetry, of which general relativity is a special case, and which may encode effective corrections from an underlying quantum theory of gravity. Focusing on spherically symmetric black holes and cosmological spacetimes in theories in which vacuum spacetimes display bounded curvature invariants, we derive the conditions under which regular geometries can be supported by static and perturbative scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids. We discuss the impact of matter on the regularity requirements of curvature boundedness and geodesic completeness relative to vacuum, finding in general that coupling to matter does not eliminate the existence of theories with regular solutions.

title: Efficient Analysis of Numerous Galactic Compact Binaries via the Free-bin Scheme
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures. Published in Physics Letters B
summary: Global analysis of Galactic compact binaries (GCBs) for space-based gravitational-wave detectors is computationally demanding in the high-frequency region (above $\sim$10 mHz), where resolvable signals are sparse but frequency samples are numerous. We propose a free-bin scheme that evaluates the nontrivial likelihood only in movable frequency windows centered on sampled signal frequencies. The method preserves the joint-likelihood structure by replacing only the signal-containing regions of a precomputed null likelihood, and avoids the fixed-bin edge effect by construction because the windows follow the sampled frequencies. In a simulated TianQin dataset containing 193 GCBs, 192 injected sources are recovered with waveform fitting factors above 0.99. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that the free-bin and conventional full-band likelihood implementations yield identical results when the same finite-length local waveforms and numerical settings are used. Computational benchmarks show that the acceleration is primarily controlled by the fraction of the frequency domain covered by the merged signal windows and decreases as this coverage increases.

title: A Relativistic Newton's Third Law for Binaries in Environments
summary: We derive the relativistic form of Newton's Third Law governing the interaction between intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and surrounding relativistic matter fields. Working within a two-parameter expansion, we rewrite the evolution of the secondary's orbital elements in a form resembling the integrated forces acting on the environment, avoiding the need to calculate any gravitational perturbations sourced by the dynamical matter content. Using the retarded and advanced Green's functions, we obtain both instantaneous and orbit-averaged laws relating the rate of change of the secondary's orbital energy and angular momentum to that of the matter and the gravitational-wave fluxes at that order. Our results clarify and correct the mixture of ad hoc balance prescriptions currently employed in the literature, providing first-principles forcing functions for the secondary's orbital elements in two ready-to-use forms: a leading-order formulation suitable for fast evaluation with complex relativistic matter simulations, and a first-post-adiabatic formulation of the energy and angular-momentum evolution in environments that are stationary and axisymmetric at leading order.

title: Effective theory of quantum black holes with Kretschmann scalar
comment: 12 pages, 15 figures, under review in European Physical Journal C
summary: We investigate the thermodynamics, quasinormal modes (QNMs), and shadows of the effective theory of quantum black holes (BHs) by expanding the physical constants in terms of the Kretschmann scalar. The resulting effective metric can contain two horizons, which is typical for a quantum-corrected Schwarzschild spacetime. The second-order corrected metric only shifts the first-order corrected metric, allowing investigation of IR phenomena from the pure first-order corrected one. From a thermodynamic point of view, the metric leads to a stable cold remnant with zero entropy, compatible with the third law of thermodynamics. In the perturbation regime, we use massless scalar perturbations to extract the effective potential, QNMs, graybody factor, and total absorption cross section. We show that double-horizon BHs have a double light ring in the potential, and for a certain value $\Omega/\chi^2=0.01,$ the QNMs are similar to the GR case since the horizon is Schwarzschild-like. We also tested the correspondence between the QNMs and the graybody factor, and our results still hold with an error far below $1\%$. Our results also conclude that the higher the frequency, the bigger the cross-section area. For the optical observables, we observe that the opposite sign of $\Omega$ leads to distinct behavior of the BH's photon sphere and shadow radius. The Sagittarius A* shadow radius upper bound from the Event Horizon Telescope observation in the $2\sigma$ and $1\sigma$ significance set the upper limit of the quantum parameter $\Omega$ to $\Omega/\chi^2 \lesssim 0.3649$ and $\Omega/\chi^2 \lesssim 0.0105$, respectively.

title: Coronagraphic time-delay interferometry: fundamental steps towards concrete applications
summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a future space-based gravitational wave (GW) observatory. Central to LISA data analysis is time-delay interferometry (TDI), which reduces otherwise overwhelming laser frequency noise. In previous work, we explored coronagraphic TDI, a sky-dependent null-stream channel which cancels the GW signal of a point-like source when pointed at its sky position. Because this property relies only on the geometric response of LISA, coronagraphic TDI is a candidate for model-agnostic sky localization. Here, we address three challenges which arise when analyzing realistic LISA data: (i) spacecraft motion; (ii) signal superposition; (iii) instrumental noise. We derive a second-generation coronagraphic TDI variable and its analytic noise model, and show that it reduces laser frequency noise in the presence of spacecraft motion while still recovering the position of the source. Using pairs of Galactic binaries (GBs), we find that sources can be localized independently provided they do not overlap in frequency, even when they share the same sky position, whereas sources overlapping in frequency can only be localized if one dominates by a factor of ~100 in amplitude. This is confirmed by the analysis of a simulation containing a massive black hole binary and 49 verification GBs. Finally, we introduce a statistical test based on the analytic noise model, which provides well-calibrated confidence regions for the sky position of the source. Applying it to GBs in the presence of instrumental noise, we find that the geometric response alone only weakly constrains the sky position: even at signal-to-noise ratios of order 10^4, 90% confidence regions span ~10^3 deg^2. These are fundamental steps towards applications of coronagraphic TDI to LISA data, such as sky localization and glitch discrimination, which we discuss.

title: Diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic LISA stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
summary: Simultaneous global-fit inference of the numerous sources observed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) depends on accurate modeling of its stochastic components: instrumental noise, the Galactic foreground, and astrophysical or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWB). Realistic features such as non-Gaussian transients and data gaps challenge traditional likelihood-based pipelines, creating an opportunity for simulation-based inference (SBI) to augment traditional analyses. Here, we present an SBI framework for LISA stochastic component separation built on the Simformer, a transformer trained with diffusion or flow matching that ingests the full time-delay interferometry cross-spectral matrix via a physics-aware embedding. We progressively relax standard simplifying assumptions on simulated 11.6-day datasets containing a loud foreground and a faint power-law SGWB. With unequal arms and per-link noise freedom, the networks match 17-dimensional MCMC posteriors after importance reweighting; full cross-spectra constrain each link's optical metrology noise amplitude to $1\%$. When marginalizing over glitches or massive black hole binary transients, estimation errors remain flat up to transient signal-to-noise ratios of several hundred, whereas ignoring them severely biases likelihood fits. Under time-varying spline noise levels, realistic glitch rates, and gaps up to one day long, posterior coverage remains nominal or conservative across $\sim 10^4$ simulations. We test coverage in the local neighborhood of a given observation by introducing a novel importance-weighted localized simulation-based calibration test. We find flow matching slightly better calibrated than diffusion in simpler regimes and observe modest gains from physics-aware template inputs. Finally, we outline how these networks can initialize the noise and stochastic blocks of a LISA global fit.

title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
summary: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS fluxes. Deriving the BMS charges requires additional care, since BMS generators extended into the bulk are generally not tangent to the null hypersurfaces. After accounting for this and the associated anomalies, the renormalized canonical charges still contain an additional soft contribution. The prescription of a covariant boundary Lagrangian determines a corner improvement that removes this term and recovers the standard BMS charges.

title: The Kerr Metric in Canonical Harmonic Coordinates to All Orders
comment: 36 pages. Codes available at Github this https URL and Zenodo this https URL
summary: We give in closed form the transformation from Boyer--Lindquist coordinates to the canonical harmonic coordinates of the Kerr metric, to all orders in Newton's constant and in the spin. This is the canonical harmonic chart selected by the MPM prescription and by the harmonic-gauge Einstein recursion sourced by the Kerr multipoles, with the residual homogeneous freedom fixed by the boundary conditions. The chart is the real, time-reversal-covariant combination of the two radial harmonic functions underlying the Cook--Scheel coordinates, which differ from it by a definite residual harmonic transformation. The proof rests on a classification of the residual harmonic freedom. Rotational covariance, parity, time reversal and analyticity in the spin allow a decaying homogeneous solution beyond the linear field only in the spatial components at third post-Minkowskian order, with angular degree $\ell=p+2$ at spin order $a^p$. This sector is a pure gauge mode, equivalent to an MPM gauge moment. The exact chart selects the representative in which this third-PM homogeneous mode vanishes; imposing the same condition on the recursion removes the only residual ambiguity and fixes its solution uniquely. As a consequence, the canonical MPM iteration needs no finite-part regularisation and no harmonicity correction at any order. We give the exact gothic metric and the post-Minkowskian coefficients in closed form through fifth order, where an arctangent function first appears at fourth order. We find agreement with recent canonical MPM and amplitude-based results at fourth order, and we verify the construction in exact arithmetic through fifth order and twelfth order in the spin, with code made publicly available.

title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
summary: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.

title: Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases
summary: Finding bases of Feynman integrals whose differential equations are suitable for phenomenology is a remarkably verifiable task. We exploit this to design two \emph{skills} with which Claude Opus~5.5 produces novel results autonomously, working for several days. For a two-loop five-point family (with two masses and 18 elliptic sectors) and a two-loop superfamily for the radiative jet function with a K3 sector, the agent finds bases whose differential equations are free of poles in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ and at most quadratic in it, and takes the jet-function one to $\varepsilon$-factorized form.

title: The cosmological lithium problem and how decaying relics still solve it
summary: Lithium-7 in old stars is about three times below the prediction of standard big-bang nucleosynthesis, and deuterium lies slightly above it. Precise measurements of deuterium, helium-4, and the effective number of neutrino species now disfavor most previously proposed particle solutions. We find that relics that decay or evaporate with lifetimes of a few hours, mostly into electron antineutrinos of about a hundred MeV and into electrons or photons, still lower lithium-7 while respecting these measurements. Such relics include gauge bosons of $L_e-L_\tau$ or $B-3L_e$ and heavy neutral leptons with a dipole coupling or mixing with $\nu_\tau$, with masses of a few hundred MeV, and populations of evaporating Q-balls that carry lepton number. The decaying particles substantially alleviate the lithium problem, while Q-ball populations reach the $2\sigma$ range of lithium-7 adopted by the Particle Data Group. These relics can shift the effective number of neutrino species by up to about $2.5$ times the precision expected from the Simons Observatory, and a future Galactic supernova can test the particles.

title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
summary: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

title: Dijet production in $e^+e^-$ collisions at NNLO+PS accuracy
summary: We present the first complete Monte Carlo event generator with next-to-next-to-leading order QCD accuracy for lepton collisions. The approach is based on a new formulation of the MiNNLO formalism and is applied to dijet production. Starting from the resummation of the three-jet resolution variable $y_3$, we present the corresponding MiNNLO master formula and implement it within the Powheg framework. We discuss phenomenological results relevant for LEP and future electron-positron colliders.

title: Exploring Screening Masses of Light and Heavy Spin-$3/2$ Baryons in a Symmetry Preserving Contact Interaction Model
comment: 19 pages, 12 figures. Accepted for publication in PRD, 2026
summary: We present a study of the screening masses of spin-$3/2$ baryons within a symmetry preserving contact interaction framework. Extending previous finite-temperature investigations of light baryons, we analyze 16 systems composed of $u$, $s$, $c$, and $b$ quarks, including light, heavy-light, and fully-heavy configurations with both positive and negative parity states. Whenever available, our results are compared with previous contact interaction calculations and other theoretical predictions. Our analysis shows that the screening masses generally increase with temperature, while the thermal evolution of the relative splitting between positive and negative parity states exhibits a clear dependence on the flavor content. Although a reduction of the relative parity splitting is observed in most channels, this behavior is not universal. Nevertheless, the uncertainties associated with the screening masses allow the parity partners to approach more closely at high temperatures, remaining compatible with an enhanced tendency toward parity degeneracy. Thermal modifications are strongest in the light sector and become increasingly suppressed as the heavy-quark content grows. To characterize this evolution, we introduce characteristic temperatures associated with the onset of thermal effects and find a general tendency for strong thermal modifications to occur at comparable or slightly higher temperatures in the negative parity channel. We further analyze the corresponding Faddeev amplitudes and show that the dominant diquark correlations remain clearly identifiable throughout the temperature range considered. These results provide a unified description of light and heavy spin-$3/2$ baryons and offer new insight into the flavor dependence of their thermal evolution and the persistence of quark--diquark correlations in hot QCD matter.

title: Study of Radiative Muon Capture Experimental Data and its Implications for Muon-Conversion Experiments
summary: Radiative muon capture (RMC) is an important background in searches for the neutrinoless conversion of a muon into an electron in the field of a nucleus, and in particular in searches for the lepton flavor and lepton number violating process of muon-to-positron conversion. The high-energy tail of the RMC photon spectrum remains theoretically understudied, leading to large uncertainties in background predictions for upcoming muon-conversion experiments. In this work, we revisit previously published RMC data to investigate improved modeling of the high-energy tail. We develop a model characterized by distinct nucleon-knockout final states, each with its associated multibody phase space and kinematic endpoint. This framework is applied to photon data from TRIUMF and positron data from SINDRUM II, and the results are compared to the previously used closure approximation. We find that separately modeling the distinct nucleon-knockout final states provides an improved description of the available RMC data near the endpoint, and we discuss the implications for the COMET and Mu2e experiments.

title: Unstable particle collisions in space and time
summary: A proper quantum description of colliding beams reveals the spacetime structure of collision processes, going beyond the conventional picture of classical point-like particles undergoing short-distance scattering. This familiar picture emerges as an approximation in the classical beam limit and under specific conditions. Resolving the t-channel singularity in processes initiated by an unstable particle requires going beyond the short-distance treatment because this singularity is associated with a long-distance effect: the decay of the unstable particle, followed by the propagation of its decay products until they scatter with the other beam. In this article, we develop the theory of spacetime collisions to allow the systematic study of the classical expansion accessing quantum corrections, and we apply it to unstable-particle collisions.
